conventions.convention: Reaction-inward rectangles have finite endpoints a_i < b_i, nonnegative reaction components on lower faces, and nonpositive components on upper faces. Inwardness is a hypothesis distinct from flow invariance.
The periodic grid uses cell-center samples, N_j ≥ 3, positive heat stencil A_h, and diffusion generator -d_r A_h, with d_r ≥ 0 and equal node weights equal to the cell volume.
No-flux TPFA omits boundary conductances. Interior conductances are symmetric and nonnegative; M has cell volumes on its diagonal and diffusion is generated by -d_r M^{-1}L_h.
Stoichiometric vectors are nonnegative; conservation or dissipation is required throughout the specified state set. Discrete mass uses the stated positive cell/node weights.
The Euler reaction restriction is τ ≤ min_{L_i>0} 1/L_i; the minimum is +∞ when every coordinate Lipschitz constant is zero.
Lie splitting applies reaction first and exact specieswise diffusion second. Approximate subsolver errors are outside the guarantees.
Continuous mass balance on boxes and tori is choice-free; the specified finite piecewise C1 domain branch assumes AC_omega and homogeneous Neumann data off the surface-null edge set.
The no-flux Cartesian stencil replaces missing neighbors by the boundary cell value. Reflection doubles each grid count using index k ↦ 2N_j-1-k on the reflected half.
Turing instability tests actual spatial eigenvalues strictly inside the open unstable band; band endpoints have a zero eigenvalue and are not Hurwitz.

load_bearing.statement: For either stated finite diffusion system, each species evolution matrix has nonnegative entries and row sums one, contracts the maximum norm, preserves component intervals for all t ≥ 0, and preserves each weighted species sum.

For a reaction-inward rectangle R and F continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood with derivative bounded on some closed neighborhood, each initial state in R has a unique solution for every t ≥ 0 remaining in R; conservation vectors preserve c^Tz and dissipation vectors make it nonincreasing.

For reaction-inward R and the stated coordinate Lipschitz constants L_i, z + τF(z) lies in R for z ∈ R and 0 ≤ τ ≤ τ_R; the step preserves conservation-vector mass and decreases dissipation-vector mass.

For F ∈ C2 near a compact reaction-inward rectangle R and a C1_t C4_x periodic solution in R, exact reaction-then-diffusion Lie iterates initialized by samples and using τ=T/N satisfy max_{0≤n≤N} ||U^n-P_hu(t_n)||∞ ≤ C_T(τ+h_max²), with C_T independent of grid widths and N.

For each C4 periodic component, the positive centered stencil plus sampled Laplacian has absolute error at most (1/12) sum_j h_j² ||∂_jjjj u_r||∞; uniformly bounded fourth derivatives give a mesh-uniform O(h_max²) sampled residual.

For u taking values in compact R with bounded spatial derivatives through order two and F ∈ C2 near R, ||A_h F_h(P_hu)-DF(P_hu)A_h P_hu||∞ is bounded uniformly over the stated periodic grids and times, where A_h is the diffusion generator.

Assume tr J < 0, det J > 0 and d_1,d_2 > 0. At each actual spatial eigenvalue λ ≥ 0, J-λD has a positive-real-part eigenvalue exactly when q(λ)<0, is Hurwitz exactly when q(λ)>0, and has a zero eigenvalue when q(λ)=0. A continuously available unstable band exists exactly when β_T>0 and β_T²>4d_1d_2 det J.

published_dependencies.used_for: Positive periodic centered heat stencil and its sign convention.
Exact periodic Fourier eigenvalues and completeness of grid modes.
Local reaction-flow existence and uniqueness; uniqueness of finite linear diffusion and FEM evolutions.
Maximal reaction solution used in the compact-rectangle continuation argument.
Zero rectangle violation and Lipschitz stability of reaction flows.
Integrated reaction mass identities, coordinate diffusion cancellation, difference estimates and finite-dimensional variation of constants.
Coordinatewise integration of continuous Laplacian terms on boxes.
Diffusion mass cancellation on the specified finite piecewise C1 domains under AC_omega.
Exact finite-face, outward-normal and surface-null-edge hypotheses for the general-domain mass balance branch.
Explicit AC_omega assumption in the piecewise C1 domain branch.
Fourth-derivative remainder estimate establishing second-order centered-stencil consistency.
Checked the hypotheses inherited by the Taylor corollary, including the reflected formula for negative increments.
Integrability of continuous first-derivative expressions in the commutator proof.
Bounds on first-derivative differences without assuming continuity of second derivatives.
Continuity of first derivatives when second derivatives exist in the commutator lemma.
Finite diffusion exponentials, positivity construction, variation of constants, reflection intertwining and FEM solution differentiation.
Positive scalar exponential factor in the diffusion positivity proof.

seams_checked.note: Opened the supplier page, def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh and def-tpfa-harmonic-face-scheme. The consumer retains the supplier's outward shared-face flux sign, positive symmetric harmonic transmissibilities and cell-volume weights. It explicitly replaces Dirichlet boundary fluxes by zero boundary flux, derives its own conservative generator, and makes no general-mesh accuracy or mimetic positivity claim. The Cartesian specialization gives the same interior transmissibilities and omits boundary contributions.
